items.followUp: Give one difference between aerobic and anaerobic respiration and state one product of each.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration takes place in the presence of oxygen, while anaerobic respiration takes place without oxygen.
rubric.description: Distinguishes the processes by their oxygen requirement.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the oxygen requirement of both processes.

rubric.why: Aerobic respiration produces carbon dioxide and water; anaerobic respiration produces lactic acid in muscles or ethanol in yeast.
rubric.description: States the products of aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the aerobic products and at least one correct anaerobic product.

modelAnswer: Aerobic respiration occurs in the presence of oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water.
Anaerobic respiration occurs without oxygen; it produces lactic acid in muscles, or ethanol and carbon dioxide in yeast.

items.followUp: Write two common symptoms of a peptic ulcer.

rubric.why: Pain or a burning sensation in the stomach is a common symptom of an ulcer.
rubric.description: States stomach pain or a burning sensation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct pain symptom.

rubric.why: Nausea, vomiting and indigestion may also occur with an ulcer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one additional correct symptom.

modelAnswer: Common symptoms of an ulcer include pain or a burning sensation in the stomach.
Other symptoms may include nausea, vomiting or indigestion.

items.followUp: State two dietary or lifestyle factors that can cause constipation.

rubric.why: Eating too little fibre or roughage can cause constipation.
rubric.description: Identifies insufficient fibre or roughage in the diet.

rubric.why: Drinking too little water, lack of exercise or ignoring the urge to defecate can contribute to constipation.
rubric.description: Identifies another common cause of constipation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one additional correct cause.

modelAnswer: Constipation may be caused by eating too little fibre or roughage.
It may also result from drinking too little water, lack of exercise or ignoring the urge to defecate.
